items.question: Which columns does the CSV have, in what order, and under what header names?
items.ticket: download their requisition list (with status and fill counts) as CSV
items.chose: Writes the header 'Requisition ID,Title,Status,Openings,Filled,Created' with the columns in that order.
items.instead: Use snake_case or field-name headers, or leave out the Created column or add other columns.

items.question: How are the rows ordered?
items.chose: Sorts a copy of the input by createdAt ascending, then by id compared by code unit.
items.instead: Keep the caller's input order, or sort newest first.

items.question: What does the CSV contain for an empty list?
items.chose: Returns the BOM and the header row only.

items.question: Does the output start with a UTF-8 byte order mark?
items.instead: Emit plain text with no BOM.

items.question: Which line terminator does the CSV use, and is there a trailing newline?
items.chose: Ends every row, including the last, with CRLF.
items.instead: Separate rows with LF, or leave off the final newline.

items.question: How are fields containing commas, quotes or line breaks escaped?
items.chose: Wraps the field in double quotes and doubles any inner quotes (RFC 4180). It does nothing else, including no neutralising of leading =, +, - or @ (formula injection).
items.instead: Also prefix fields that start with =, +, - or @ to block spreadsheet formula injection, or always quote every field.

items.question: What is written for a missing or null title?
items.instead: Write a placeholder such as '(untitled)', or throw.

items.question: How is the creation time formatted?
items.chose: Writes the full ISO 8601 UTC timestamp from toISOString(), with milliseconds.
items.instead: Write a date only (YYYY-MM-DD) or a locale-formatted date.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has a status outside open, on_hold, filled or cancelled?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the requisition id and the status, and the whole export fails.
items.instead: Write the raw status string, or skip the row.

items.question: Are zero openings accepted, and what counts as a valid openings value?
items.chose: Accepts 0 and any non-negative integer. It throws for negative, fractional, NaN or infinite values.
items.instead: Require openings of at least 1, or pass the number through unchecked.

items.question: What happens when the filled count is invalid or greater than openings?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id if filled is not a non-negative integer or is greater than openings.
items.instead: Clamp filled to openings, or export the value as it is.

items.question: What happens when a requisition has an invalid creation time?
items.chose: Throws an Error naming the id if createdAt is not a Date or is an invalid Date. One bad row fails the whole export.
items.instead: Write an empty Created field, or skip the bad row.
